Paginating the List

skip/take turn a page number into a slice of rows; the controller turns the total row count into meta.

Still getAllTickets (Figure 3.13): skip: (page - 1) * pageSize, take: pageSize. Prisma's findMany doesn't know about "pages" — only skip (how many rows to leave out at the start) and take (how many to return after that). Page 1 skips nothing ((1 - 1) * 10 = 0); page 2 skips the first 10 ((2 - 1) * 10 = 10) and takes the next 10; page 3 skips 20, and so on — the same idea as Laravel's ->skip()->take() or ->paginate() under the hood, just spelled out by hand here instead of a query builder method doing it for you.

findMany (the page of rows) and count (how many rows match where in total, ignoring skip/take) run inside one Promise.all([...]) rather than two separate awaits — both queries are independent of each other, so there's no reason to wait for one to finish before starting the other; this is the same "run independent async work concurrently" idea from Lesson 1's async topic, just with two Prisma calls instead of two arbitrary promises.

The controller turns that total into the pagination meta the response envelope (first topic) actually sends:

// Figure 3.14: building the meta object (src/controllers/ticket.controller.js, excerpt)
export const getAllTickets = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  const { page, pageSize } = req.query;
  const { tickets, total } = await ticketService.getAllTickets(req.query);

  sendCollection(res, tickets, {
    page,
    pageSize,
    total,
    totalPages: Math.ceil(total / pageSize),
  });
});

page and pageSize come straight back off req.query — already validated numbers, defaults and all, thanks to validate.js replacing req.query with Zod's parsed result (Figure 3.5). totalPages is the one value nothing upstream computed yet: Math.ceil(total / pageSize) rounds up, since a total of 25 with a pageSize of 10 needs 3 pages, not 2.5 — a client can now tell from meta alone whether there's another page worth requesting, without needing to guess from whether the current page came back full.
